_comment: THE IMAGE THE MEASUREMENT RUNS IN, PINNED BY DIGEST AND NOT BY TAG.
A tag is a POINTER and the person who can move it is not this repository. Every other input to this
authority is named by content - the authority is checked out by SHA, the candidate is checked out by SHA
and re-read with git rev-parse, the runner command comes from a protected enum, the mutation matrix is a
committed file - and the image is the filesystem the measurement's interpreter, its libc and its git come
out of. An image named `node:22.22.3-bookworm` is a sentence about whatever Docker Hub serves under that
name at the moment the run starts, which is exactly the floating input the interpreter pin exists to
deny. So the digest is the pin; the tag beside it is a human label and nothing checks it.
WHY THIS IMAGE AND NOT THE SLIM ONE. The measured suite shells out to `git` - this repository's own
fixtures build ephemeral repositories to measure against - so an image without git turns a whole class of
tests red for a reason that has nothing to do with what they test. node:<v>-bookworm derives from
buildpack-deps:bookworm-scm and carries git; node:<v>-bookworm-slim does not. The preflight probe in
measure-terms.mjs checks BOTH the interpreter version and git inside the pinned image before any
measurement runs, and refuses the run rather than reporting a suite that failed for want of a binary.
UPDATING THIS PIN is a commit on this repository, reviewed like any other change to what this authority
runs. Resolve the new digest, read what changed, and update the tag label in the same commit.
